lines: Open your department’s Weather Alerts page, then select
Settings beside View History.
This training department currently says there are no active weather alerts.
The Settings page opens Notification Settings, which describes the
controls for automatically generating messages to department members.
This lesson prepares and checks those policy settings.
Practice in a separate training department before changing how a
live team receives information.
Review Enable Weather Alerts and Minimum Severity to Display.
The enable checkbox stays clear throughout this exercise.
Change the display selection from Moderate to Severe.
The help below says that only alerts at or above the selected severity
will be shown in the dashboard.
This is the display threshold.
The separate table below controls which severities generate automatic
messages, so review both areas when deciding your department’s policy.
Scroll to the complete Auto-Message Severity Threshold table.
It provides Extreme, Severe, Moderate, Minor and Unknown rows, each with its own
Enabled checkbox, Start Hour and End Hour.
Every Enabled box remains clear here.
The Extreme row contains eighteen and six: the help explains that this
wraps overnight, from six P M to six A M in department local time.
Delivery includes the start hour and excludes the end hour.
Zero and twenty-four represent all-day delivery.
Entered hours alone do not check a row’s Enabled box.
Review Excluded Alert Events below the table.
The help asks for a comma-separated list of event titles that should not generate
automatic messages, and says those alerts can still appear in the dashboard.
This example retains only a clearly fictional Practice alert title.
Treat exclusion as a deliberate messaging decision, not as a way
to remove an alert from every view.
Agree the appropriate event titles with your department
before changing a live policy.
Below the exclusions, find Attach Weather Context to Calls.
Its help says that enabling it attaches active weather alerts near
a call’s location as a call note.
Keep it unchecked in this training exercise.
Consider whether that context belongs in your department’s incident record
and review the resulting notes when you test an operational configuration.
This recording changes no call notes; it shows the actual
option and its stated purpose.
Select Save Settings for the prepared policy.
Reload Settings and look at Minimum Severity to Display
again: Severe remains selected.
Enable Weather Alerts is still unchecked.
That fresh readback confirms the threshold was stored beyond the
earlier unsaved dropdown choice.
It does not demonstrate a received weather alert or a delivered message.
Verify the saved controls and any operational results separately.
Return the display selection to Moderate and select Save Settings again.
The page shows Settings saved successfully beside the button.
Reload once more: Moderate is retained, and global Enable
Weather Alerts remains clear.
Scroll through the full severity table to confirm its unchecked
rows and retained hours.
Then review the unchanged fictional exclusion and
unchecked call-context control.
This leaves the original disabled training policy in place.
The Alert Sources notice says no weather alert sources are configured.
Saving notification policy does not establish a live feed.
Source setup and a verified alert are separate work before operational use.
Search-and-rescue teams, wildland contractors, industrial emergency teams
and security departments can all benefit from an agreed weather-information policy,
as can community paramedicine, mental health response, fire and E M S teams.
Choose the display and messaging behavior that supports your operations, then
test the complete configured service.
